Shape multi-site digital transformation
About the Company:
Our client is a leading Hospitality organisation with a diverse portfolio of operations, committed to innovation, operational excellence and investing in technology that enables business performance and long-term growth.
About the Role:
We are seeking an experienced IT Systems Manager from the hospitality industry to lead the strategy, governance and delivery of enterprise systems across a multi-site environment. You will oversee system architecture, implementation, compliance and vendor management while ensuring technology solutions are secure, scalable and aligned with business objectives.
Key Responsibilities:
Lead the implementation and life-cycle management of enterprise systems.
Develop and maintain systems governance, standards and architecture.
Oversee major system upgrades, integrations and technology projects.
Ensure compliance with cyber security, risk and regulatory requirements.
Manage technology vendors and implementation partners.
Drive continuous improvement, automation and system optimization.
Partner with business and IT stakeholders to deliver strategic technology outcomes.

Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science or a related discipline.
8–10 years' experience managing enterprise systems in complex environments.
Proven experience delivering multi-site systems implementations.
Strong background in systems architecture, integration and governance.
Experience managing technology vendors and project delivery.
Exposure to Microsoft Dynamics 365, Shiji or similar enterprise platforms is highly regarded.
Strong leadership, stakeholder engagement and strategic decision-making skills.

and submitting your most recent CV in Microsoft Word format.

27901.description:
Surveyor
HBS (PNG) LIMITED
currently operates in numerous mine sites across PNG, both on the mainland and remote island locations. We own and operate one of the largest and best maintained mining fleets in PNG, offering the mining sector a variety of services including road construction and maintenance, haulage, lighting and crushing services and plant equipment hire.
We are taking expressions of interest for highly and suitably qualified individuals for the position of
Surveyor
. Applicants must have experience within the mining and construction fields.
This role will involve:
Survey and Set-Out Activities
Conduct and maintain accurate survey control and set out works to ensure construction activities align with approved designs and specifications.
Data Collection & Monitoring
Collect, monitor, and analyze survey data to track project progress, earthworks quantities, and compliance with design requirements.
Quality Assurance
Verify survey accuracy and completed works to ensure compliance with project standards, tolerances, and quality requirements.
Planning and Coordination
Coordinate with project teams to support construction schedules, resolve survey issues, and facilitate efficient project delivery.
Safety, Health & Environment (HSE)
Adhere to all HSE requirements and promote safe surveying practices while identifying and reporting workplace hazards.
Reporting
Maintain accurate survey records and provide timely reports and data to support project management and progress tracking.
The Candidate must have:
Demonstrated 3-5 years of surveying experience in large-scale civil earthworks, mining, dam construction, or other heavy industrial projects.
Proven ability to deliver accurate survey outcomes in challenging terrain using modern surveying technology and in coordination with construction teams and heavy equipment operators
Bachelor's Degree or Advanced Diploma in Surveying from a recognized institution.
Valid PNG Class 3 or 6 Driver's Licence, with ASPNG membership or eligibility considered an advantage.
Advanced technical expertise in survey equipment, UAV/drone surveying, data analysis, and engineering software such as Surpac, Deswik, and AutoCAD Civil 3D.
Strong safety focus, problem-solving ability, resilience, and communication skills to perform effectively in demanding, multicultural project environments.
A competitive remuneration package will be negotiated based on applicant’s experience and skills.
CANDIDATE MUST BE LAE-BASED
If you have what we are looking for, please send in your application with your CV and all relevant documents to:
The Recruitment Team
HBS (PNG) Ltd
P O Box 958
LAE 411
Fax: 475 8348
[email protected]

Apply

27900.description:
Earthwork Supervisor
HBS (PNG) LIMITED
currently operates in numerous mine sites across PNG, both on the mainland and remote island locations. We own and operate one of the largest and best maintained mining fleets in PNG, offering the mining sector a variety of services including road construction and maintenance, haulage, lighting and crushing services and plant equipment hire.
We are taking expressions of interest for highly and suitably qualified individuals for the position of
Earthwork Supervisor
. Applicants must have experience within the mining and construction fields.
This role will involve:
Lead and supervise all earthworks and civil construction activities, ensuring excavation, filling, grading, compaction, roadworks, embankments, and backfilling are completed safely, efficiently, and to project requirements.
Coordinate personnel, subcontractors, equipment, and resources to achieve production targets while maximizing productivity and minimizing operational downtime.
Ensure compliance with project drawings, specifications, survey controls, quality standards, and engineering requirements, including material placement and compaction standards.
Monitor project progress and performance, maintaining accurate records, reporting production outcomes, and proactively resolving field issues impacting safety, quality, schedule, or productivity.
Promote a strong safety and environmental culture through toolbox meetings, workforce communication, HSE compliance, risk management, and adherence to permit and environmental conditions.
Collaborate effectively with Surveyors, Engineers, QA/QC, HSE personnel, clients, and stakeholders to support inspections, audits, construction coordination, and successful project delivery.
The Candidate must have:
Extensive earthworks supervision experience in mining, infrastructure, roads, dams, TSF, or heavy civil construction projects, with strong leadership of crews and equipment fleets.
Proven technical capability in earthworks operations, survey interpretation, construction planning, productivity management, and delivery in challenging terrain conditions.
Bachelor's Degree or Advanced Diploma in Surveying (or equivalent relevant qualification) from a recognized institution.
Valid PNG Class 3 or 6 Driver's Licence, with ASPNG membership or registration eligibility considered advantageous.
Strong technical expertise in earthworks construction, heavy equipment management, quality control, survey interpretation, environmental compliance, and productivity monitoring.
Effective leadership and interpersonal skills, including safety leadership, team management, communication, decision-making, problem-solving, resilience, and accountability.
A competitive remuneration package will be negotiated based on applicant’s experience and skills.
CANDIDATE MUST BE LAE-BASED

28098.description:
SPECTRA
LAE
IS HIRING
– LICENSED ELECTRICIAN
!
Spectra Industrial Limited - a Leader in Sales, Service and Hire of Forklifts, Gensets and Industrial Supplies, is seeking an organized, qualified, and well experienced Licensed Electrician to join our Lae Workshop Team and be a part of our growing enterprise!
Position Description
Position Title: Licensed Electrician
Company: Spectra Industrial Limited
Location: Lae, Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea
Reports To: National Electrical Manager
Position Purpose
The Licensed Electrician will be responsible for installing, testing, diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining electrical systems, wiring, controls, equipment, generators, motors, workshop facilities, construction sites, solar PV and battery storage installations, and site electrical assets to ensure safe, reliable, and compliant operation. Applicants must hold a recognized electrical trade qualification and a current electrical license, with strong practical experience, sound safety awareness, and the ability to complete electrical maintenance records accurately.
Key Responsibilities
Electrical Installation, Testing
& Preventive Maintenance
Carry out electrical installation, inspection, testing, servicing, and preventive maintenance on workshop facilities, equipment, gensets, forklifts, and related electrical systems.
Perform scheduled and breakdown maintenance in line with company procedures, manufacturer requirements, and applicable PNG electrical and workplace safety standards.
Identify faulty, unsafe, or worn electrical components and recommend timely repair, isolation, replacement, or upgrade.
Electrical
Fault Diagnosis & Repairs
Diagnose faults in electrical circuits, control panels, starters, alternators, batteries, lighting, wiring, motors, and associated systems.
Repair, replace, terminate, and test defective electrical parts and components using correct tools, test instruments, and safe electrical work practices.
Conduct post-repair testing and confirm equipment is electrically safe, functional, and ready for operation before handover.
Tools,
Test
Equipment
& Materials
Care
Use electrical tools, meters, insulation testers, manuals, drawings, and diagnostic equipment correctly and safely.
Maintain tools and test equipment in good working condition and report damaged, expired, or unsafe equipment promptly.
Assist with ordering, collection, and proper use of electrical parts, cables, consumables, and materials.
Safety, Compliance & Housekeeping
Comply with company safety procedures, PPE requirements, lock-out/tag-out requirements, toolbox talks, and Papua New Guinea workplace safety standards.
Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free workshop and work area, especially around live, isolated, or stored electrical equipment.
Report hazards, electrical incidents, unsafe equipment, and non-conformances promptly to the supervisor.
Documentation & Reporting
Complete job cards, inspection checklists, electrical test records, service reports, and maintenance records accurately and on time.
Record parts used, work completed, isolation status, test results, and outstanding repairs clearly for workshop tracking.
Communicate equipment status, defects, risks, and maintenance priorities to supervisors and relevant teams.
Teamwork & Operational Support
Work closely with mechanics, operators, stores, workshop staff, and site teams to meet operational requirements.
Assist apprentices or junior staff with safe on-the-job guidance where required and within company procedures.
Undertake additional duties, training, or site support as reasonably directed by management.
Breakdown & Field Support
Respond to workshop or field electrical breakdowns and carry out repairs efficiently to minimize downtime.
Support site-based electrical maintenance activities where travel, call-out, or roster work is required.
Ensure repaired electrical systems and equipment are safe, tested, compliant, and ready for operation.
Key Competencies & Skills
Electrical fault-finding and diagnostic ability.
Strong safety awareness and compliance with safe electrical work practices.
Attention to detail, workmanship, and accurate testing.
Communication and reporting skills.
Teamwork, reliability, and initiative.
Ability to work under pressure, respond to breakdowns, and meet operational deadlines.
Qualifications & Experience
NEA Licensed Electrician is preferred.
PPL License is acceptable, provided the applicant is willing to sit for the NEA License.
Minimum 10 years’ experience as a Licensed Electrician.
General construction experience is required.
Generators and motors operation, service and maintenance experience is highly preferred.
Exposure to Solar PV and Battery Storage installations is highly desirable.
Ability to read electrical drawings, manuals, and specifications, complete workshop documentation, and work independently or as part of a team.
Current and valid PNG driver’s license is required – Class 6 or relevant license is required.
References’ contact details must be stated in the CV.
Interested in joining our Competitive, Responsive and Committed Team?
Send your updated resumes with contactable referees, trade certificate, electrical license copy, driver’s license copy, and relevant supporting documents to email:
[email protected]
with “Licensed Electrician – Lae” on the subject line.
Applications can also be hand delivered to our Lae branch Office.
Attention: HR Recruitment Team
Spectra Industrial Ltd
P.O. Box 94, Lae 411
Morobe Province
Remuneration will be discussed during the interview.
Applicants must state current and verifiable referees’ contact details in their CV. Any references and qualifications provided will be verified and checked should your application get to shortlist stage.
Note:
Applications are open to PNG citizens only.
Priority will be given to Lae based applicants.
Former applicants need not re-apply.
Female applicants are encouraged to apply.
Application closes on COB Tuesday 25
th
August 2026.
Late applications will not be accepted.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

28096.description:
Geotechnical Engineer
Simberi Gold Company Limited’s operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Geotechnical Engineer
to join our Mine Technical Service team in a permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Simberi Island, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Senior Geotechnical Engineer, the Geotechnical Engineer will provide geotechnical support and services to Mine Technical Service, Mining and other operational teams at Simberi. The Geotechnical Engineer will assist with maintaining a minimum safe standard for all personnel, infrastructure and equipment on site as well as identifying and implement business improvement through problem solving, innovation and technology. In addition, they will assist with ensuring the geotechnical systems and procedures are implemented, employed and maintained to mitigate geotechnical hazards to the site.
Everyone at St Barbara Limited is required to understand and act in accordance with St Barbara’s Values, Code of Conduct and all Company Policies and meet all relevant internal and external compliance obligations.
The opportunity
Technical accountabilities
Support the development, implementation, review, and continuous improvement of Geotechnical Management Plans to ensure safe, sustainable, and compliant mining operations.
Perform key geotechnical engineering functions, including mine plan and schedule reviews, slope and wall design assessments, excavation compliance inspections, geotechnical mapping, data collection, monitoring, stability analysis, design recommendations, and QA/QC activities.
Identify, assess, report, and manage geotechnical hazards and risks, implementing monitoring systems and control measures to maintain safe operating conditions.
Communicate geotechnical risks, hazards, and operational issues effectively to mine personnel and management, ensuring timely awareness and appropriate mitigation measures.
Participate in and lead geotechnical investigations and projects to evaluate slope stability and establish design criteria that support the safe and efficient extraction of resources from existing and future mining areas.
Provide technical geotechnical support to mining operations through collaboration with internal departments and external stakeholders, while ensuring compliance with relevant legislation, regulations, and company safety standards.
Contribute to major hazard management processes, including the preparation of reports and the communication of geotechnical risk information to operational teams, management, and other stakeholders.
Assist in the planning, implementation, and review of geotechnical programs related to ground control, slope stability, geotechnical monitoring, and mine infrastructure to support operational performance and risk management
Scheduling accountabilities
Managing effective use of available resources, including own time, in support of the delivery of the team/crew.
People accountabilities
Support Senior Geotechnical Engineer with geotechnical data collection to maintain a high standard of monitoring and reporting.
Assist with the training and development of the team including graduate engineers and geologist.
Ensure own work performance meets all role requirements.
Manage your professional learning and development to develop in current role and for future roles.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Bachelor’s Engineering Degree in Geotechnical, Mining Engineering or Geology
At least four (4) years relevant work experience in an Open Pit Geotechnical Engineering role.
Working knowledge of mining software, preferably Deswik
Demonstrated ability to work effectively within a team
Attention to detail and a high level of accuracy in your work
Strong communication skills, problem solving skills and analytical skills
Ability to work to tight deadlines on multiple tasks
High level of enthusiasm for the work with high performance goals
You must have a strong commitment to health, safety and environmental standards
Ability to plan and work effectively and efficiently and with a minimum of supervision
A high level of written and verbal communication skills
Maintain the highest level of punctuality and attendance and be prepared to accept responsibility
For further information on the
Simberi Operations
and to apply for this role, please visit:
https://www.livehire.com/job/stbarbara-png/T4AH8
Closing date: Tuesday, 25 August 2026 at close of business.
Please submit your Applications, CVs, and Supporting documents (all merged in one PDF document)
At Simberi Gold Company Limited, we’re committed to finding the best fit for every role. We are a diverse and inclusive workplace, welcoming diversity in all its forms. All qualified applicants will be given equal consideration, regardless of their race, national origin, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity.
Apply

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners of the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives, which include educational scholarships, agricultural support and health outreach programs, help to improve quality of life and build long-term capacity in local communities.
About the role
This position leads the Business Development Section within the Community Affairs Department, providing strategic and operational support on landowner business development. The role works closely with Finance and Contracts teams to facilitate fair and transparent contract opportunities for landowner umbrella companies, while also supporting broader local enterprise growth through training and mentoring.
Key Accountabilities
This role will provide strategic advice and operational support to the K92 Management Team on all matters relating to landowner business development and participation. Part of the responsibilities include:
Lead Business Development Operations:
Manage the Business Development (Community Affairs) Section, oversee daily functions, and ensure alignment with company policies and delegated authority.
Strategic Planning & Advisory:
Provide input into departmental goals, develop strategies, and support the implementation of MOA-aligned business development initiatives.
Landowner Engagement & Project Support:
Negotiate and collaborate with Landowner Umbrella Companies to identify and implement viable economic projects.
Governance & Capacity Building:
Promote strong financial management and control systems within landowner businesses to support sustainable development.
Office Oversight & Budget Management:
Supervise the Kainantu-based Business Development Office and monitor performance, budgets, and financial targets.
Team Leadership & Development:
Lead, coach, and evaluate team performance while ensuring Development & Localization targets are met.
Compliance & Values Commitment:
Uphold workplace safety, security, human rights, and anti-fraud standards, and remain flexible to meet operational needs.
About You
To be considered for this position, candidates must have substantial experience working with resource project landowners in Papua New Guinea. In addition to this, candidates should also be able to demonstrate and have some or all of the following:
Tertiary qualifications in Business, Commerce, or a related discipline.
PNG Driver’s license Class 6 is essential
Strong financial and business management skills, with experience in budgeting, cost control, and operational improvement.
Sound knowledge of business development frameworks and legislation, including the PNG Companies Act (1997).
High-level communication skills in English and Tok Pisin, with the ability to engage rural and village-based communities.
Proven interpersonal and negotiation skills, with cultural sensitivity and the ability to build trust with diverse stakeholders.
Demonstrated leadership capability with strengths in decision-making, change management, and team performance.
Strong professional ethics, personal integrity, and a proactive approach to continuous improvement.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

Crowne Plaza Residences – Port Moresby
Where journeys meet. Connections unfold.
Our guests’ most memorable experiences begin long before they reach the Front Desk.
At Crowne Plaza Residences – Port Moresby, we are looking for an exceptional Front Office Manager whose standard is 5 star, whose instinct is personal and whose leadership is visible.
This is a role for someone who is genuinely guest obsessed. Someone who notices the details others miss, anticipates needs before they are expressed and understands how to turn an ordinary interaction into a lasting memory.
Front Office is not simply where guests check in and check out. It is the centre of the guest journey and the heartbeat of our hotel.
The opportunity
As Front Office Manager, you will take ownership of the complete guest journey, from before arrival through to departure and beyond.
You will be visible during peak arrivals, present in the lobby, engaging with guests and working alongside your team. You will know the day’s arrivals, departures, VIP guests, IHG One Rewards members, returning guests, special occasions and long stay residents. You will ensure preferences are understood, promises are followed through and every important detail is communicated across the hotel.
This is not a position for someone who wants to manage from behind a desk. Your place is where the guest experience is happening.
When the lobby is busy, you step in. When a guest needs help, you take ownership. When the experience falls short, you lead the recovery. When a process is not working, you address the cause rather than accepting the inconvenience as normal.
Dare to Connect
Crowne Plaza’s branded service style, Dare to Connect, is built around genuine human connection.
We want our colleagues to use their personality, judgement and initiative to create meaningful connections with guests. As Front Office Manager, your responsibility is to create an environment where this happens naturally and consistently on every shift.
You will coach colleagues in the moment, build confidence and empower the team to make thoughtful decisions. You will set high standards while ensuring the service remains warm, personal and unscripted.
You will lead a culture where guests receive professional attention and personal recognition, not rehearsed lines or transactional service.
Understanding the residences experience
Our hotel welcomes both short and long stay guests, and delivering excellence requires an understanding of how different those journeys can be.
For a short stay guest, every moment must feel seamless, efficient and personal. There may be only a few opportunities to create an impression, so each one matters.
For a long stay guest, the relationship develops over weeks or months. Trust is built through consistency, recognition, discretion and follow through. Their apartment becomes their home, and our colleagues become part of their daily experience.
You will ensure the team understands when to engage, when to give space and how to recognise individual routines and preferences without making the service feel intrusive. You will build genuine relationships with residents and ensure recurring concerns are resolved at their source.
Shaping the future guest journey
A major part of this role will be working with IT and hotel leaders to introduce new systems and processes that improve the guest experience.
You will help map the guest journey, identify friction points and translate guest needs into practical system requirements. You will participate in selecting, testing and implementing new technology, support the team through each launch and ensure new systems become part of how we operate rather than another forgotten login.
This may include improvements to guest profiles, preference management, communication, service requests, issue tracking, arrival preparation and the sharing of information between departments.
You must be comfortable testing workflows, identifying gaps, documenting procedures, training colleagues and measuring whether a new system has improved the experience.
Technology should remove friction and give our colleagues more time to connect with guests. It should never replace genuine hospitality.
Leading operational excellence
You will lead the daily Front Office operation with discipline, precision and a strong sense of ownership.
You will review arrivals, departures, room readiness, special requests, billing instructions, guest history and important stay information. You will conduct regular inspections of Front Office and public areas and take immediate action when something is not right.
You will work closely with Housekeeping, Engineering, Food and Beverage, Reservations, Sales, Security, Transport and IT to ensure the guest experiences 1 connected hotel rather than separate departments.
You will personally support complex service recovery, ensure complaints are resolved promptly and use guest feedback to improve how we operate. You will monitor Guest Love, online reputation, loyalty recognition and recurring service themes, turning feedback into clear actions for the team.
You will also maintain strong controls around billing, credit, cashiering, room inventory, night audit and guest information. You will support forecasting, budgeting, workforce planning, upgrades and upselling while never allowing revenue activity to feel forced or compromise the guest relationship.
As a senior operational leader, you will be ready to act as Manager on Duty and take confident leadership during an emergency or crisis.
Developing an exceptional team
Exceptional guest experiences are created by engaged and confident colleagues.
You will recruit, train, coach and develop a Front Office team capable of delivering at the highest level. You will establish clear expectations, provide regular feedback and ensure every colleague has the knowledge, tools and authority needed to succeed.
You will recognise strong performance, address gaps promptly and create meaningful development opportunities. Your leadership will reflect IHG’s commitment to giving colleagues Room to Belong, Room to Grow and Room to Make a Difference.
You will lead from the front, remain calm under pressure and never ask the team to do something you are not prepared to do yourself.
What you will bring
You will have proven Front Office leadership experience within a 5 star hotel or respected international brand. You may already be a successful Front Office Manager or an exceptional Assistant Front Office Manager ready to take full ownership of the function.
You will ideally have at least 5 years of progressive Front Office or guest services experience, including at least 2 years in a leadership position. Previous IHG experience would be an advantage, although a genuine understanding of premium hospitality and a strong record of guest service excellence are more important.
You will have strong working knowledge of a hotel property management system such as OPERA or OPERA Cloud. Experience with guest relationship systems, digital communication platforms, loyalty programmes and guest feedback tools will be highly regarded.
Importantly, you will be able to demonstrate experience implementing a new system, process or operating standard and successfully gaining team adoption.
You will be commercially aware, operationally disciplined and confident interpreting guest experience results, occupancy information, forecasts and departmental performance.
You will communicate clearly, build relationships easily and remain composed when the pressure is on. You will have an exceptional eye for detail and a reputation for following through.
Above all, you will care deeply about people and hospitality
.
What you can expect from us
At IHG Hotels & Resorts, our purpose is to deliver True Hospitality for Good.
You will join an international hotel company that believes in creating inclusive teams, celebrating difference and giving colleagues the support and opportunity to grow.
You will have access to IHG learning and development, global career opportunities, hotel accommodation discounts and the chance to make a visible difference within a distinctive residences operation.
Ready to create something memorable?
If your idea of Front Office is a desk, this is probably not the role for you.
If you see Front Office as the centre of the guest journey, a place where relationships are built, standards are protected and memorable experiences are created every day, we would like to hear from you.
Please apply with your CV and a short cover letter describing 1 bespoke guest experience you personally created and 1 new system or process you successfully implemented to:
[email protected]
Applications close at COB on Monday, 24th August 2026
Go Further Together with Crowne Plaza Residences – Port Moresby.
This vacancy is open to PNG citizens only. IHG is an equal opportunity employer. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
Apply

28119.description:
NEWMONT Technician, Mechanical (43544)
Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea | National Opportunity | 28 Days On / 14 Days Off Rotating Day & Night Shift Roster
WORK WHERE IT MATTERS
At Newmont, people create the value in the metals we mine and are ambassadors in the communities where they live and work. As the world's leading gold company and a producer of copper, we are committed to creating value and improving lives through sustainable and responsible mining.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Reporting to the Shift Supervisor Mechanical, the Technician, Mechanical plays a critical role in maintaining the reliability, availability and safe operation of Newmont Lihir's auxiliary mobile equipment fleet. This fleet includes CAT 992/988/966 loaders, CAT 18/24 graders, CAT 320/336/390 excavators and CAT D10/D11 dozers, which support loading, earthworks, road maintenance, dig face preparation, drainage activities and overall mine productivity. As part of a high-performing maintenance team, you will perform planned, preventative and breakdown maintenance activities, undertake diagnostics and fault finding, complete component change-outs and repairs, and ensure all work is carried out safely and to OEM standards. You will work closely with operations and maintenance personnel to maximise equipment availability and support the achievement of production targets. You will also support continuous improvement initiatives through technical problem solving, equipment reliability improvements, defect elimination activities and the application of best-practice maintenance techniques. Working in accordance with Newmont's Fatality Risk Management (FRM) standards and Work Management processes, you will contribute to achieving safe, reliable and efficient fleet performance. This position operates on a 28 days on / 14 days off rotating day and night shift roster and is open to Papua New Guinea Nationals only.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
-- Perform routine, planned and breakdown maintenance on auxiliary heavy mobile equipment.
-- Conduct inspections, diagnostics and fault-finding activities.
-- Execute component change-outs and repairs in accordance with OEM standards.
-- Complete SAP notifications, work orders and maintenance records.
-- Perform lubrication, fluid sampling and contamination control activities.
-- Identify equipment defects and contribute to equipment reliability improvements.
-- Support maintenance planning and scheduling activities through technical input and feedback.
-- Maintain compliance with Newmont FRM standards, critical controls and site safety requirements.
-- Work collaboratively with operations, planning and maintenance teams to maximise equipment availability.
-- Support the development of apprentices and less experienced technicians through knowledge sharing and mentoring.
ABOUT YOU
-- Trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Diesel Mechanics or equivalent.
-- Demonstrated experience maintaining large-scale mining auxiliary equipment.
-- Strong hydraulic, electrical, powertrain and mechanical diagnostic skills.
-- Experience interpreting OEM manuals, schematics and technical documentation.
-- Experience using SAP or other CMMS maintenance systems.
-- Strong commitment to safety, teamwork and continuous improvement.
-- Ability to work effectively in a diverse team environment.
-- Current PNG Driver Licence.
WHY NEWMONT
Join a global mining leader committed to safety, inclusion, sustainability and operational excellence while working at the world-class Lihir operation. At Newmont, you'll have the opportunity to build a rewarding career while contributing to a safe and high-performing maintenance team.
To Apply
To apply for this job simply click on the blue "Apply" button below.  If you prefer to use email instead, please send your CV and other relevant documentation to
[email protected]
.  Please include the Job ID "
#28119
" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.
Apply

From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods.  The Renew Project, funded by DFAT, aims to delivering reliable, clean energy to five remote, off-grid schools in North Bougainville, Papua New Guinea
Here your skills will be valued
Role Purpose
Reporting to the REnew Pacific Project Manager in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (AROB), the REnew Pacific Construction Engineer is responsible for the quality assurance and technical coordination of civil, structural, and electrical construction activities associated with the installation of mini-grid solar systems in schools in Bougainville. The role will ensure that all infrastructure works are completed safely, on time, within budget, and in compliance with applicable engineering standards, donor requirements, environmental and social safeguards, and local/national regulations. The REnew Pacific Construction Engineer will also work in close collaboration with Construction Electrical Services (CES) Ltd., which will provide the solar facilities for each school.
Key Areas of Accountability
Program Planning and Design
Review and validate site assessments, engineering designs, drawings, and technical specifications in collaboration with CES ensuring safety and quality.
Assess school infrastructure to determine readiness for solar installations and identify any required remedial works in collaboration with CES.
Verify structural adequacy of rooftops and mounting locations for solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in collaboration with CES and propose adjustments as needed / feasible.
Contribute to project implementation plans, schedules, budgets, and procurement specifications, helping to ensure plans are realistic to ensure safe, quality structural works.
Support the preparation of Bills of Quantities (BOQs), technical scopes of work, and tender documentation, providing technical input as needed for all relevant procurement.
Construction Supervision
Supervise contractors and subcontractors undertaking construction and installation activities including CES and other subcontractors as needed / relevant.
Monitor progress against approved work plans and construction schedules and communicate issues as and when they arise, offering technical advice as relevant.
Ensure construction works comply with approved drawings, technical specifications, and quality standards, highlighting any challenges as they arise.
Conduct regular site inspections and document progress through reports, photographs, and field records.
Verify quality and quantity of works completed prior to approval of contractor payments.
Solar Infrastructure Oversight
Coordinate installation of solar PV systems, battery storage, inverters, electrical distribution systems, and associated infrastructure in collaboration with CES.
Ensure all solar installations comply with relevant electrical and safety standards.
Verify system commissioning, testing, and performance prior to handover together with CES.
Support development of operation and maintenance procedures for installed systems and collaborate with CES to provide training and coaching to Energy Focal Points.
Quality Assurance and Compliance
Implement quality control and quality assurance procedures throughout project execution in line with global technical standards and national / local regulations.
Ensure that all structural works are compliant with project environmental, social, health, and safety requirements.
Monitor contractor adherence to workplace health and safety standards.
Address/ highlight technical issues and recommend corrective actions where necessary.
Ensure all project documentation is complete and properly maintained in line with donor requirements and Save the Children policies and procedures.
Stakeholder Coordination
Liaise with school administrators, community leaders, government counterparts, contractors, suppliers, and project partners, particularly CES.
Facilitate site meetings and technical coordination sessions in collaboration with CES.
Support community engagement activities related to construction and related project activities, particularly with respect to facility operation and management.
Represent the project during technical inspections and stakeholder consultations and provide technical input / information during donor and senior management visits.
Co-facilitate and assist with community, committee and school meetings as needed.
Reporting and Documentation
Prepare weekly and monthly progress reports.
Maintain construction records across the entire cycle, ensuring that all records are well maintained and audit friendly.
Contribute technical inputs to donor and management reports, including photos as relevant.
Identify risks related to infrastructure, environmental and social safeguards, resource management, and compliance, and work with the project team to proffer mitigation measures.
Work with the country office to ensure that adequate controls are in place across construction activities to mitigate against loss, mismanagement or theft.
Capability Building
Provide technical mentoring to contractors, technicians, and project staff where appropriate.
Co-facilitate and assist with training of Energy Management Committees, Focal Points, and school representatives on infrastructure maintenance and management.
Promote local workforce participation and skills development.
General
Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.
Embody the Save the Children values in practice of Accountability, Ambition, Collaboration, Creativity, and Integrity. Work according to Save the Children’s mandate and child focus.
Work according to any other duties as assigned by the individual’s supervisor.
Child protection and safeguarding requirements
Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.
Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s
Child Safeguarding Policy
,
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.
Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behavior towards children in private and professional life.
Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.
Maintain a safe and positive relationship at all times when working with children and young people.
Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.
Health, safety, security and risk management
Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training. Act safely at all times.
Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.

At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.

It takes all types of people to do the challenging work we do. Here are some of the specific skills and experiences you’ll bring in this role:

Bachelor’s degree in in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Registration with a recognized professional engineering body is desirable. Strong knowledge of construction management principles and engineering standards.
Minimum five (5) years of relevant engineering and construction supervision experience – particularly in solar infrastructure. Demonstrated experience managing infrastructure projects in remote or challenging environments.
Demonstrated experience with renewable energy, solar PV systems, electrical infrastructure, or rural electrification projects. Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and technical documentation.
Experience working with donor-funded development projects, NGOs, government agencies, or international organizations is an advantage.
Knowledge of occupational health and safety requirements.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and construction reporting tools. Experience using AutoCAD or similar engineering software is desirable.
Excellent leadership and team management skills.
Excellent writing and verbal skills in English for reports and communications documents. Ability to present complex information in a succinct manner. Proficiency in Tok Pisin.
Proven ability to work effectively with government and diverse partners and stakeholders at all levels from regional to community, and

K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Project Support Officer – Arawa Based
CARE International in PNG is looking into recruiting a suitable candidate for a Project Support Officer role based in Arawa, ARoB. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.
CARE International in Papua New Guinea has a focus on Gender Equality, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Agriculture and Health.
Reporting to the Operations Coordinator and Program Manager, the Project Support Officer (PSO) is responsible for providing effective administrative, logistics, travel, accommodation, asset, inventory and office support services primarily for the Arawa field office with additional support to Buka office. The role ensures that office systems, travel arrangements, vehicle use, stores, assets, visitors, meetings and workshop logistics are well coordinated and compliant with CARE PNG policies, donor requirements and internal procedures. The position works closely with program, finance, procurement, safety and security, ICT and administration teams to enable timely, safe, cost-effective and accountable delivery of program activities in Bougainville. This position is based in Arawa, with possible travel to field sites and other CARE PNG locations as required.
The PSO has four direct reports and is expected to organize staff and resources towards achieving objectives effectively and efficiently. This role is based in Arawa but will require travel throughout North, Central and South Bougainville.
This Position will have indirect contact with Children or vulnerable adults.
EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS:
Minimum technical diploma and/or vocational training in Business Administration, Logistics, Supply Chain Management or another related field, and/or minimum three years’ relevant experience in administration and logistics functions, preferably with an international non-government organisation or private company.
Demonstrated experience in office administration, logistics coordination, travel support, accommodation bookings, fleet support, inventory control and supplier coordination.
Demonstrated experience following standard policies, procedures and processes and ensuring accurate documentation for routine transactions and operational activities.
Ability to organise workload, meet deadlines, solve problems, exercise sound judgement and work under pressure in a busy field office
Good interpersonal, communication, negotiation and coordination skills, with the ability to work respectfully with staff, partners, suppliers, visitors and community stakeholders.
Demonstrated honesty, reliability, trustworthiness and ability to maintain
Ability to contribute to team objectives and work effectively in a group
Willingness to learn about CARE, gender equality, women’s empowerment, safeguarding, PSEAH and locally led development
Fluent communication skills in Tok Pisin and intermediate oral and written
Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel, with good numeric and record-keeping
The closing date for this position is Monday 24h August 2026

Collaborating with internal and external stakeholders across multiple properties and countries.

Bachelor's Degree in Human Resources Management, Employment Relations, Industrial Relations, or a related discipline.
Minimum 5 years' experience in a senior Human Resources leadership role, preferably within hospitality, International group or a multi-site environment.
Demonstrated experience partnering with senior leaders to deliver commercial business outcomes through people strategies.
Excellent coaching, influencing, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills.

High level of integrity and ability to maintain strict confidentiality.

Sponsorship is available for this role

Competitive salary and benefits package.
Global career development and learning opportunities.
Hotel discounts across IHG Hotels & Resorts worldwide.
A collaborative, inclusive, and people-first culture.
The opportunity to shape the future of hospitality across Fiji and the Pacific.

- Ability to work independently and follow instructions precisely.

27925.description:
GROUP OPERATIONS MANAGER
HBS (PNG) LIMITED
currently operates in numerous mine sites across PNG, both on the mainland and remote island locations. We own and operate one of the largest and best maintained mining fleets in PNG, offering the mining sector a variety of services including road construction and maintenance, haulage, lighting and crushing services and plant equipment hire.
We are taking expressions of interest for highly and suitably qualified individuals for the position of
Group Operations Manager
. Applicants must have experience within the mining and construction fields.
Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO). The role is responsible for leading the safe, profitable, and efficient delivery of HBS operations across Papua New Guinea while supporting the Company's strategic growth objectives and overall business performance.
The position provides leadership across mining, civil infrastructure, oil and gas, maintenance, equipment management, and future diversified service offerings, ensuring operational excellence, strong financial performance, high client satisfaction, and full compliance with contractual, regulatory, and corporate governance requirements.
Working closely with the COO and Executive Leadership Team, the Group Operations Manager is accountable for integrating operational delivery with commercial, financial, project controls, asset management, supply chain, human capital, and business development functions to maximise profitability, optimise resource utilisation, effectively manage operational risk, and deliver sustainable business growth.
The Candidate must have:
Minimum 20 years' progressive leadership experience, including at least 10 years in senior operational leadership roles, within mining, civil infrastructure, oil and gas, EPC/EPCM, maintenance, or integrated mining services, with responsibility for multi-site operations and overall business performance.
Demonstrated experience leading complex operations in Papua New Guinea or similar remote and developing operating environments, including the management of multicultural workforces, remote logistics, stakeholder engagement, and client delivery. Previous operational leadership experience in Papua New Guinea is strongly preferred.
Experience working with Australian and/or international resource sector clients, with a strong understanding of Tier 1 contractor expectations, governance, commercial practices, and project delivery models. Fixed term contract up to 07 August 2027 (with possible extension)
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to PNG and International candidates
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.
The program aligns with the broader goals of the
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, which emphasises locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as
PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
.
This Opportunity
As
Scholarships Strategy Lead (Strategic Direction)
you work with Department of Higher Education Research, Science and Technology (DHERST) to implement programme design, policy development, institutional partnerships, systems strengthening, and strategic oversight appropriate for scholarship program. This will include:
Provide strategic advice on scholarship selection criteria, outreach approaches and award management processes.
Design long-term strategic plans and policy frameworks for the different TVET scholarship modalities. Including working with the Disability Specialist, supporting the implementation of the disability policy issues.
Align educational investments with PNG national development plans and SWLT EOPO (e.g., PNG Vision 2050, PNG National Higher and Technical Education Plan).
Identify and build institutional linkages between SWLT, training colleges, TVET partner institutions and private sector employers.
Maintain ongoing relationships with DHERST Scholarship Division, other aid programs and regional partners (e.g., DFAT, PAS, ITVET4E)
Facilitate co-funding models and apprenticeship pipelines with major industries and pivot scholarship quotas toward high-demand sectors (e.g., agriculture, renewable energy, trades).
Analyse labour market data, economic forecasts, and industry trends to identify critical skill gaps for scholarships.  Identify priority fields of study and target groups based on labour market analysis and workforce development needs
Develop targeted equity policies ensuring access to TVET for women, persons with a disability, rural and remote students and disadvantaged students to increase participation from underrepresented groups.
System Stewardship and Governance, provide strategic oversight of the entire TVET scholarship ecosystem, including governance arrangements, policy coherence across modalities, risk management, and quality assurance of partner institutions to ensure scholarships deliver credible and nationally recognised outcomes.
Sustainability and Financing Strategy, lead long-term sustainability planning for TVET scholarships beyond donor cycles, including diversified financing models, cost-effectiveness analysis, employer cost‑sharing, and transition pathways for increased PNG government and industry ownership.
Support the integration of scholarship activities with broader education, TVET and workforce development initiatives
Prepare strategic reports, briefing notes and recommendations for program management for key stakeholders.
About you
You will demonstrate proven experience in the following areas:
Demonstrated experience in the design and delivery of scholarship programs and management of scholarship support systems
Strong understanding of workforce development, labour market and skills development priorities
Strategic thinking and ability to align scholarship investments with broader development objectives
Demonstrated program management experience with an ability to initiate and manage program activities in a development context, and with deep understanding of financial management and compliance requirements
Excellent interpersonal skills, including verbal and written communication, and ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with a range of internal and external stakeholders including partner government counterparts
Experience integrating GEDSI considerations into scholarship initiatives including experience working on programs that promote inclusive and diverse access would be advantageous
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team.
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
Skills in Technical and Vocational Education and Training or understanding of the TVET sector and TVET Colleges in PNG – desirable
To Apply
Please submit your application online, including your CV and brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position through

28049.description:
Plumber
The licensed, no-leaks kind
Location:
Atlas, Port Moresby
Employment:
Full-time, Local Hire
Important:
If you do not have proven plumbing experience, a recognised trade qualification, and the required plumbing or drainage licence—or eligibility to obtain one—please do not submit your CV.
Atlas is part of the Kenmore Group of Companies and supports projects across steel fabrication, modular housing, building, and civil works.
We’re looking for an experienced and licensed Plumber to join our Port Moresby team and deliver high-quality plumbing work across Steel Haus modular homes, construction projects, fabrication works, and project sites.
This is not a role for someone who cuts corners, hides leaks, or leaves defects for someone else to fix.
We need someone who can read plans properly, complete accurate rough-ins, install fixtures neatly, test every system, and deliver plumbing work that is compliant, reliable, and ready for handover.
If your experience is limited, this is not the job to practise on.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for installing, testing, commissioning, and maintaining water supply, sanitary, drainage, stormwater, and hot-water systems.
That includes setting out and installing cold and hot-water pipework, waste, soil and vent lines, sanitary fixtures, tapware, cisterns, tanks, pumps, and hot-water systems.
You’ll complete rough-ins and fit-offs across steel-framed buildings, modular homes, and active construction sites without compromising structural or waterproofing integrity.
You’ll also install sanitary and stormwater drainage to the correct levels and falls, including trenching, bedding, connections, and backfilling.
Where required, you may work on septic systems, rainwater tanks, on-site wastewater systems, solar hot-water units, and instantaneous hot-water systems.
Every installation must be pressure-tested, leak-tested, commissioned, and completed in line with approved drawings, project specifications, AS/NZS 3500, and applicable PNG building requirements.
You’ll work closely with site supervisors, fabrication teams, electricians, project teams, apprentices, and trade assistants to coordinate work and avoid clashes, delays, and rework.
The expectation is simple: install it properly, test it properly, and leave no defects behind.
Who This Suits
This role suits an experienced, qualified Plumber who takes pride in producing clean, compliant, and handover-ready work.
You should have a recognised plumbing trade qualification and a current PNG plumbing or drainage licence, trade registration, or the ability to obtain one.
You understand plumbing drawings, hydraulic plans, construction specifications, pipework systems, drainage falls, fixture installation, testing, commissioning, and defect rectification.
You should have at least three to five years of post-qualification experience across residential, commercial, modular, or construction plumbing.
Experience working to Australian Standards, particularly AS/NZS 3500, will be highly regarded.
You must be able to work independently, plan your tasks, manage materials, maintain accurate records, and complete work with minimal supervision.
You are reliable, safety-focused, physically capable, and comfortable working on active construction sites, in trenches, confined spaces, at heights, and in tropical conditions.
If people already rely on you to make sure the plumbing is right the first time, this role will feel familiar.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
Atlas is involved in real construction, steel fabrication, modular housing, building, and civil works projects.
You’ll work across a variety of projects where quality workmanship directly affects the finished product and the reputation of the business.
This is a role where good tradespeople are valued, safety is taken seriously, and defect-free work matters.
There may also be opportunities to travel to Lae and other project sites as required.
How to Apply
If you’re reading this and thinking, “I install it properly and leave no leaks behind,” then we want to hear from you.
Send your CV, cover letter, copies of your trade qualifications, and relevant licences to:
HR Team

Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is in the National Capital District, and Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. 27717.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is part of a team responsible for the implementation and maintenance of the mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and exploration sites in Kainantu.  In addition, this position will also play and important role in the training of trades assistants.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you are a NATTB certified electrician, with PPL certification and demonstrated experience within a mining / minerals processing environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Experience in installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control Centre’s, LV and HV transfers and starters.
The ability to fault find and develop appropriate solution in order to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Good health physical ability is a prerequisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

Zenag Chicken has pioneered the poultry industry in Papua New Guinea for over 75 years. We provide employment to over a thousand employees, with our Head Office based in Lae and our farm a few hours’ drive out of the city, along the Bulolo District.
Due to expansion, we are hiring a
Layer Production Supervisor - Farm Based.
The successful candidate will work in our Commercial Layers Farm, reporting to the Commercial Layers Manager. Responsibilities include managing and oversee workforce, shed management, animal health and flock performance, whistle ensuring to best practices and procedural adherence.
Duties and Responsibilities includes
Supervising daily layer production activities and workforce allocation.
Monitoring bird health, welfare, and flock performance
Ensuring effective shed management and adherence to operational procedures.
Ensuring feed, water, lighting, and ventilation programs are implemented correctly.
Provide guidance and training to team members on best practices.
Supervise staff attendance, rostering, and performance
Providing support to the Commercial Layers team to complete any activity and tasks.
Adhering and following all company policies and SOP
Requirements:
Must have at least 2 years in supervisory role and working experience in Agriculture or Poultry industries.
Must have a degree in Agriculture or related fields.
Must have strong leadership skills
Must have excellent communication skills and teamwork ability.

[email protected]
. Application must be attention to Human Resource Manager.
Please note, ONLY short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews
Closing date of submission 18
th
August 2026

27832.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our growing exploration department, you will be responsible for the day-to-day coordination of general administration of the Exploration Department and supporting the management team.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Provide general administrative support to Department Manager and staff team.
Undertake general administrative duties including, general word processing, filing, copying, and faxing.
Keep and maintain records or file system of workers’ administrative matters
Minute taking for board/in-house meetings, collation and distribution of minutes, department weekly and monthly reports, and other documents.
Dealing with incoming and outgoing mails.
Ordering of office equipment, materials, and stationeries.
Obtaining quotes to raise purchase orders for stationeries as and when required.
Updating inventory on office supplies and equipment.
Attend to reservations for flights/travels and accommodation for employees.
Monitor and update weekly workplace inspection log sheet
Preparation of timesheets every pay period ending
Usual administration procedural activities.
Update of shift and work rosters.
May possibly require working extended hours.
Attend to other administrative duties in line with role and as instructed by immediate Supervisor.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
A Diploma or Certificate in Business Administration, or equivalent.
5 year’s work experience in mining environment or similar.
Well versed in various areas of travel (domestic/international, business, corporate group, individual etc)
A self-starter, very resourceful and with ability to finding solutions.
Proficiency in English; knowledge of additional languages is an advantage.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Proficient in computer and e-mail correspondences and courteous.
Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.
Strong planning and organizational skills.
Ability to present, persuade and communicate effectively.
Demonstrable ability to work under pressure.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO RESIDE IN EASTERN HIGHLANDS AND MOROBE PROVINCES
Apply

28031.description:
Geologist – Resource Development (241557)
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
NPL now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mineral Resources Department as
Geologist – Resource Development (241557)
.
About the role
Reporting to the Senior Resource Geologist, the Geologist – Resource Development is responsible for advancing the understanding of the mineral resource through the design, implementation and interpretation of exploration and resource definition programs. The role contributes directly to the growth, development and optimization of the resource base, ensuring data quality and integrity for robust geological modelling and resource estimation.
This position works closely with exploration, mine geology and resource geology teams to bridge early-stage geological data with mine planning and production needs.
In this role, you will:
•    Design, plan and oversee resource definition drilling programs (RC, diamond, aircore, etc.)
•    Manage and ensure high-quality geological logging, sampling and data collection
•    Interpret geological and assay data to refine geological models and mineralization controls
•    Liaise with database administrators to ensure accuracy and integrity of geological data
•    Contribute to 3D geological modelling and support resources estimation processes
•    Collaborate with exploration geologists to identify and prioritize target areas for growth
•    Generate and deliver technical reports, including resource updates, cross-sections and long sections
•    Ensure drilling, sampling and QAQC protocols meet industry and company standards
•    Support compliance with regulatory reporting requirements
•    Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
•    Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geoscience, or a related field
•    3 plus years of experience in resource development, exploration or mine geology
•    Proficient in geological and modelling software (e.g. Leapfrog, Micromine, Datamine)
•    Understanding QAQC protocols, drilling techniques and estimation principles
•    Strong analytical, communication and technical reporting skills
•    A proactive and safety conscious mindset
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Geologist – Resource Development (241557)
Embark on a rewarding career with NPL as a Geologist - Resource Development. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note
: This advert will be open until
18th, August 2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.
Apply
