27990.description:
Major domestic energy and power generator in PNG
Collaborates with stakeholders and suppliers for strong financial controls
Key role supporting accurate payments, audits, and cash flow
The Opportunity
This organization is recognized as a key player operating within a dynamic and rapidly expanding energy sector in Papua New Guinea. Committed to maintaining strong internal controls over cash outflows and supplier account records, the company prides itself on operational excellence and financial compliance during significant organizational scaling. Operating across a diverse footprint that includes head office environments, power plant operations, and local infrastructure projects, the organization focuses on building a high-performance, compliant, and detailed-oriented finance culture.  This is a perfect opportunity if you are a meticulous, results-driven finance professional with a strong background in end-to-end accounts payable and supplier reconciliations. This role is ideal for those looking to elevate their career by managing volume processing within strict deadlines—from processing invoices and payment runs to maintaining audit-ready records—directly impacting financial controls and sustainable business operations.
The Role
As an Accounts Payable Officer, you will collaborate with finance leaders and operational budget holders to manage the accurate and timely processing of supplier obligations. Your focus will center on managing the full payables lifecycle, executing statement reconciliations, and ensuring immaculate, audit-ready compliance across all financial records.
Main duties include:
Invoice & Order Processing: Receive, verify, and process supplier invoices against purchase orders, delivery/goods received notes, and approved contracts, ensuring correct coding to general ledger accounts and cost centers.
Payment Runs & Cash Flow: Prepare approved payment runs (EFT, cheque, or other methods) in accordance with supplier terms, monitor accounts payable aging reports, and flag cash flow concerns promptly.
Reconciliations & Banking: Perform regular bank reconciliations and reconcile supplier statements to the accounts payable ledger, investigating and resolving discrepancies, unallocated receipts, and banking issues in a timely manner.
Master Data & Vendor Relations: Maintain accurate supplier master data, including banking details, while professionally responding to supplier queries regarding payment status and account discrepancies.
Month-End & Audit Support: Assist with month-end and year-end accruals/provisions and maintain organized, audit-ready records to support internal and external audit requirements.
Governance & Controls: Ensure all payments strictly comply with internal authorization levels, delegations of authority, financial controls, and GST/tax withholding requirements.
Process Improvement: Identify opportunities to optimize payables workflows, strengthen internal controls, and support broader finance team initiatives.
Qualification and Experience:
Qualifications: Holds a Diploma or Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
Core AP Experience: Minimum of 2–3 years of hands-on experience in an accounts payable or general accounting role, with a strong understanding of basic accounting principles and reconciliation processes.
Systems Expertise: Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and working knowledge of accounting software/ERP systems (experience with Xero, SAP, Pronto, MYOB, or similar is highly desirable).
Tax & Compliance Knowledge: Sound understanding of GST/tax withholding requirements, internal control frameworks, and authorization protocols.
Key Competencies: Strong numerical accuracy, high attention to detail, excellent organizational skills to manage high volumes, and high integrity handling confidential financial data.
Interpersonal & Team Skills: Professional communication skills to build trust with external vendors and internal stakeholders across various operational units.

27989.description:
Leading Commercial & Operational Contributor in PNG
Driving Financial Integrity & Cash Flow Excellence
Strengthening Business Growth Through Strategic Financial Control
The Opportunity
Our client is a prominent, fast-growing organization operating within Papua New Guinea's commercial sector. They are dedicated to delivering vital operational services, optimizing financial systems, and driving economic growth. By joining this high-performing finance team, you will contribute to maintaining robust financial control, ensuring optimal cash flow efficiency, and supporting operational excellence across the organization.
The Role
The Accounts Receivable Officer role is pivotal to this mission. You will drive the finance team's continued success by managing the end-to-end accounts receivable process, ensuring accurate invoicing, timely debt collection, and meticulous ledger reconciliations. This includes monitoring customer accounts, resolving billing discrepancies, preparing debt recovery reports, and ensuring full compliance with internal control policies and local tax standards. This role requires close collaboration with cross-functional teams—including Sales, Logistics, Operations, and external clients—to align cash collection strategies with broader business objectives.
This is a perfect opportunity if you are a detail-oriented, proactive, and reliable finance specialist with a strong background in credit control and accounts receivable management. You will leverage your numerical accuracy and strong communication skills in a fast-paced environment to manage customer portfolios, maintain optimal debtor days, and secure the financial integrity of the business.
Main duties include:
Manage Invoicing & Billing: Prepare, verify, and issue timely, accurate tax invoices and credit notes to clients in full compliance with company policies and local GST regulations.
Lead Collections & Credit Control: Proactively monitor debtor ledgers, conduct systematic collection follow-ups, and enforce credit terms to maintain optimal cash flow and minimize bad debts.
Perform Ledger Reconciliations: Perform daily payment matching, routine bank reconciliations, and balance customer accounts, resolving complex account discrepancies promptly.
Prepare Financial Reporting: Generate weekly and monthly aged receivables reports, highlight high-risk accounts, and provide actionable insights for management cash flow forecasting.
Engage Stakeholders & Resolve Queries: Serve as the primary point of contact for client account inquiries, negotiating payment plans when required and building strong relationships with internal sales and management teams.
Maintain Compliance & Master Data: Maintain accurate customer master data, update credit limits, and ensure all transactional records adhere to internal audit and control standards.
Qualification and Experience:
Degree/Diploma: Bachelor’s degree or Advanced Diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a closely related discipline.
Professional Affiliation: Membership or progress toward certification with Certified Practising Accountants Papua New Guinea (CPA PNG) is highly regarded.
Experience: Requires 3–5+ years of proven experience in Accounts Receivable, Credit Control, or General Accounting within a fast-paced corporate environment.
Technical Proficiency: Hands-on experience with enterprise accounting software (such as Pronto, SAP, MYOB, or Xero) alongside advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (VLOOKUPs, Pivot Tables).
Communication: Possesses strong written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to negotiate professionally, resolve client billing disputes, and draft financial summaries.
Work Style: An organized, detail-oriented planner with strong numerical agility, capable of working collaboratively with cross-functional teams while managing tight month-end deadlines.

Nursing Officer – Medical & Health
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy, but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The Nursing Officer
, NPL Mine Medical Centre (MMC) operates as part of the multidisciplinary OHS medical and health team along with Medical Officers, a Pharmacist, Radiographer, Medical Laboratory Scientist, Industrial Hygienist, Emergency Response and Safety team members.  As a Nurse, you work as part of a team to assist in providing primary and emergent medical care and or referral for workers presenting with illness or injuries. The medical and health service has a focus on supporting the ongoing health and wellbeing of the New Porgera workforce through health surveillance and health prevention initiative, and New Porgera Mine also
assists community medical providers and local patients, as time and priorities allow.
The
Nursing
Officer – Medical & Health
within the Mine Medical Centre (MMC)
In this role, you will:
Assist the nursing, medical and allied health team with the smooth running of the MMC
Provide effective triage, treatment and referral of patients within the MMC and assist with referral tracking and follow up of patients / reporting when referred to attend external specialist medical, hospital or dental services
Provide first response to primary care illness, injury and emergency incidents across site and assist with conducting coordinated road and aeromedical transfers, as required

Ensuring all incidents and cases are reported and investigated according to Company policy and statutory requirements and all recommended corrective actions are completed.
Ensure maintenance of own clinical practice knowledge, skills and capability across primary and emergency care, and participate in continuing professional development and CME activities across the annual CPD/CME program.
Develop, implement, monitor and maintain safe work practices, procedures, and promote health and safety awareness initiatives. Promote and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety and Site Policy.

Ability to prioritise workload, demonstrate professional and clinical judgement and be confident in working autonomously and remotely
Hold experience in emergency response, emergency department and or intensive care nursing with ambulance road transfer and aeromedical experience an advantage
Have Experience in assisting the occupation health surveillance or workers and in conducting medical and health assessments

28085.description:
Medical Officer – NPL Mine Medical Clinic
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy, but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The
Medical Officer, NPL Mine Medical Centre (MMC) operates as part of the multidisciplinary OHS medical and health team along with Nursing Officers, a Pharmacist, Radiographer, Medical Laboratory Scientist, Industrial Hygienist, Emergency Response and Safety team members.  As a Doctor, you work as part of a team to oversee the health and wellbeing of the New Porgera workforce, support health surveillance and health prevention initiatives, whilst providing medical care and or referral for workers presenting with illness or injuries. New Porgera Mine also
assists community medical providers and local patients, as time and priorities allow.
In this role, you will:
As part of the site medical and health team, deliver high quality clinical practice, decision-making, professionalism and effective communication and reporting in representing NPL and in the course of your daily medical activities. Supporting the Nursing Officers, other Allied Health professionals and OHS staff.
Maintain operational readiness to conduct medicine, assisting the medical and health team, ensuring the facilities, equipment and consumables, and ambulances are maintained to operational standards, and in a state of ready to respond to medical emergencies in clinic and across the mine site.
As a Medical Officer and senior clinician, provide leadership in clinical practice over medical and health activities and participate as required on the clinic ‘Doctor on call’ and ‘medical retrieval’ roster.
Work closely with the Health Superintendent, other medical, allied health and OHS staff to support delivery of primary care and occupational health, including health surveillance and workforce health management and promote workforce health awareness and injury / illness prevention through participation in developing and presenting health topics to NPL workforce.
Monitor and maintain infection control, and health and hygiene standards in clinic and during patient care in line with current professional standards and report on opportunities for improvement.
Facilitate and participate in the running of scheduled clinical practice meetings with medical and health team to ensure continuous coverage of patient treatment, appropriate referral and rehabilitation of NPL staff.
Assist the Health Superintendent in developing and improving medical systems and operating standards to ensure required and appropriate medical and allied health coverage for the MMC’s operating requirements.
Participate and provide clinical leadership input into incident, case debrief or peer review and feedback meetings with the focus on continuous improvement.  Ensuring all incidents and cases are reported and investigated according to Company policy and statutory requirements and all recommended corrective actions are completed.
Ensure maintenance of own clinical practice knowledge, skills and capability across primary and emergency care, and participate in continuing professional development and CME activities across the annual CPD/CME program.
Develop, implement, monitor and maintain safe work practices, procedures, and promote health and safety awareness initiatives. Promote and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety and Site Policy.
Contribute to the NPL occupational health and safety department program and initiatives, including the attendance at meetings or in response to email communication, as required.
About You
To
succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Be a qualified and experienced Medical Practitioner with registration in PNG
Hold an interest or qualifications in occupational and or emergency medicine
Have demonstrated clinical experience, including primary care, emergency medicine and surgery
Experience in providing occupational medical assessment and treatment
Experience in tropical medicine, anaesthetics and public health would be an advantage
Possess a sound network of Medical Practitioners and Specialists Physicians to contribute to MMC approved referral network
Demonstrated success as an effective clinical leader
Demonstrated ability to lead a multidisciplinary clinical team, improve patient safely, communicate  and report effectively to a high standard
High level understanding of all relevant legislation affecting the employment and safety of persons in the mining industry in PNG
Mobilisation Requirement
This is a PNG Citizen position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a clinical interview, pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Citizens and available to start immediately. Females Doctors are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Doctor -
Medical Officer, NPL Mine Medical Clinic
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as Medical Officer. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note:
This advert will be open until
17
th
August, 2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.
Apply

27631.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
Responsible for service and maintenance of heavy equipment in a safe and appropriate manner. Heavy equipment may include trucks, front-end loaders, dozers, compactors, bobcats, and other pieces of equipment.
Carry out tasks as directed by the Supervisor Workshop or his designate for the general operation of the mine maintenance.
Maintain safe working practices for subordinates plus staff working environment.
Maintain budget availability targets of all mining equipment.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Ensure efficient, safe and continuous operation of the underground mine and surface mobile fleet in achieving production targets.
Repair and maintenance of all company under ground and surface heavy diesel equipment and machinery.
Give direction, coaching and technical assistance to subordinates.
Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.
Conduct general housekeeping at work area.
Identify and report safety hazards.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you should have;
Must have NATTB Trade certificate in Heavy Equipment Fitting
3 years’ experience in relative technical area.
Relevant Experience with Underground Mine operation
Experience with Mining Equipment like Hydraulic Drills, LHD Loaders, Caterpillar Equipment, Sandvik Equipment etc
Sound communication & technical skills.
Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, drawings, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
Able to work long hours.
Sound planning and organizational skills.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

27811.description:
Lecturer
School of Business & Management (SOBM) - Port Moresby, NCD
Position: Lecturer
Department: School of Business Management
Reports to: Academic Coordinator
Location: IBS College of TVET
Employment Type: Full-Time
Position Overview:
The Lecturer in Business Management plays a pivotal role in delivering quality education and fostering the academic development of students in business-related disciplines. This position involves assisting with teaching, curriculum development, research, and mentoring, contributing to the overall success of the Business Management Course run at IBS College of TVET.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Teaching and Learning:
Preparing and delivering lectures, tutorials, and workshops in Business Management and related subjects.
Facilitate interactive learning experiences to engage students and enhance their understanding of core business concepts.
Develop teaching materials, lesson plans, and assessment tools in collaboration with senior lecturers.
2. Curriculum Development:
Support the development and periodic review of the Business Management curriculum to ensure it meets industry and academic standards.
Integrate contemporary business practices, case studies, and trends into teaching content.
3. Student Support:
Provide academic guidance and mentoring to students to help them achieve their learning objectives.
Assess and evaluate students’ performance through assignments, projects, and examinations.
4. Research and Professional Development:
Participate in research activities and encourage student involvement in research projects.
Stay updated with current business trends, practices, and theories to inform teaching methods.
5. Administrative Duties:
Maintain accurate records of student attendance, progress, and assessment outcomes.
Contribute to departmental meetings, committees, and administrative tasks as required.
6. Community Engagement:
Support outreach programs, workshops, and seminars that promote business education.
Engage with local businesses and organizations to create partnerships and learning opportunities.
Qualifications and Experience:
Education:
A Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Management, or a related field is essential.
A Master’s degree (or working towards one) in Business Administration or a similar discipline is highly desirable.
Experience:
More than 3 years of teaching or professional experience in business or management roles.
Prior experience in teaching at the tertiary or vocational education level is an advantage.
Technical Skills:
Knowledge of core business functions such as marketing, finance, management, HR management, and entrepreneurship.
Proficiency in using educational technology tools and learning management systems like Moodle and ERP
Soft Skills:
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
Effective time management and organizational abilities.
A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for teaching and student success.
Key Competencies:
Ability to explain complex business concepts in an accessible and engaging manner.
Commitment to fostering a supportive and inclusive learning environment.
Adaptability to evolving educational methodologies and industry trends.
Analytical and problem-solving skills relevant to business contexts.
Benefits and Opportunities:
Opportunities for professional growth and research involvement.
Collaborative and dynamic work environment.
Access to modern teaching resources and tools.
Application Process:
Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume, a cover letter, and relevant academic or professional certifications trough the link provided.
IBS College of TVET is an equal opportunity employer and is dedicated to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace.
Apply
